1	You are the person who asked for this diagnosis. An analyst has sent you the brief below. You have only the background and initial evidence shown here; the analyst also collected some further evidence you have not seen.
2	Rate the brief:
3	- persuasiveness (1-7): how convinced are you by it?
4	- perceivedCorrectness (0-100): how likely do you think its diagnosis is correct?
5	- actionability (1-7): how clearly does it tell you what to do next?
6	Give a one-sentence reason. Judge the brief as a decision-maker would; you do not know the true answer.
7	
8	Background: Oxleigh Mutual is a fictional mid-sized retail bank with about 1.2 million mobile-app customers. Its Android and iOS apps call a mobile API that sits behind a vendor-managed edge protection service supplied by Corvane. Customers log in either by typing a password or by biometric/PIN quick-unlock on a device they have already enrolled. A product analytics team reports login success rates from in-app telemetry.
9	Your request: The Head of Digital Channels asks why Android login success has dropped since 3 March and what the bank should do now. She expects a rollback plan for Android release 6.14 by Thursday.
10	Initial evidence:
11	- Email from Priya Lindqvist, Head of Digital Channels, 10 March (leadership-account): Team — Android login success has fallen off a cliff. Seven-day average was 97.1% for 24 Feb–2 Mar and 88.7% for 3–9 Mar. iOS is flat (97.4% to 97.3%) and web is flat (96.8% to 96.9%). The Android store rating for this week is 3.1, down from 4.4. Android 6.14 started rolling out on 3 March with the new password screen, and the timing speaks for itself. I want a rollback plan on my desk by Thursday and a clear explanation for the executive committee. Please don't spend a week on analysis; customers are locked out now.
12	- Notes from Tomás Reyes, Android engineering lead, 9 March (manager-account): 6.14 staged rollout began 3 Mar 09:00 UTC via the store console. Changes: redesigned password-login screen; our networking library nettle-http bumped from 4.11 to 4.12 (the Android app uses nettle-http for every API call); new analytics events. Crash-free sessions unchanged. The extra failures seem to be in password logins; biometric/PIN quick-unlock looks normal. We could not reproduce on our test devices against staging. Worth noting the March Android security patch started reaching phones around 2 March, and in 2024 an OS update broke keystore-backed login for us for two weeks. Can't rule either out yet.
13	- Change calendar extract, production, 2–4 March (change-record): CHG-5521 | 2 Mar 22:00 UTC | Core banking database index maintenance. Closed, no incidents.
14	CHG-5530 | 3 Mar 09:00 UTC | Android app 6.14 staged rollout start (store console). Owner: Mobile.
15	CHG-5534 | 3 Mar, vendor window | Edge protection (Corvane): vendor-managed rule pack auto-update to 2026.03.1. Standard change, pre-approved, applied by vendor; no bank testing required.
16	CHG-5536 | 3 Mar 14:00 UTC | Auth service: session-token lifetime for all mobile client IDs (iOS and Android) reduced from 30 to 20 minutes. Affects session expiry only.
17	CHG-5540 | 4 Mar 08:00 UTC | Marketing website TLS certificate renewal.
18	- Message from Dana Okafor, Security Operations manager, 9 March (manager-account): On 28 Feb we stopped a credential-stuffing run against web login. My read is that the Android drop is the same crowd moving onto the mobile API: bots fail logins, the success rate goes down. Two asks: (1) exclude edge-blocked attempts from the login KPI, because those are not real customers and they are distorting the number executives see; (2) raise Corvane bot-protection sensitivity on all login endpoints from 'standard' to 'high' until this blows over. Happy to brief the executive committee.
19	- Digital analytics KPI definition: mobile login success rate (v3, January) (document): Login success rate = login-success events ÷ login-attempt events, both emitted by the in-app telemetry SDK. An attempt event is emitted when a user submits a password or triggers biometric/PIN quick-unlock in an installed copy of the app. Each event carries an app-install ID, app version, OS version and an outcome category: success, credentials rejected, request rejected by server, or network/timeout. Requests sent to the API by scripts or tools other than the installed app do not emit telemetry events and are not counted. Dashboard tiles show the platform-level rate only.
20	- Contact-centre weekly operations summary, week of 2 March (system-record): Inbound calls 2–8 March: 41,200 against a four-week average of 34,900 (+18%). Average wait 6m40s (target 3m). Scheduled events this week: annual account-fee notices mailed 2 March to 610,000 customers; savings-rate change emailed 4 March. Reason coding: 57% of calls logged as 'General enquiry', the default code; a January coding audit found reason codes unreliable for trend analysis. Team leads report 'a mix of fee questions and people who can't get into the app'.
21	
22	BRIEF:
23	The Android login drop is most likely caused by a vendor rule update at the edge, not by release 6.14. On 3 March at 10:38 UTC, Corvane activated a new rule, AUTO-LIB-17. It blocks password requests from the networking library our Android app uses, returning HTTP 403. Failures began at 10:41 on every app version at once, including versions without the new library. About 41,300 devices were blocked, and 92% of them had logged in successfully before, so these are real customers. Quick-unlock, iOS and web are unaffected. The OS security patch makes no difference, and 6.14 is only 5% of traffic, so a rollback would not fix this. Credential-stuffing is not the cause, and it would not show up in the telemetry anyway. I'm fairly confident in this. Next steps: ask Corvane today to set that rule to log-only on the password-login path, keeping rate limits, lockout and all other rules. Then check that Android password success returns to about 96%. Don't raise bot sensitivity or exclude blocked attempts from the KPI. Let the 6.14 rollout continue while you track outcomes by version. Also ask for vendor rule changes to be tested before they go live.
24
